newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe stocks weaker but set to recover.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe stocks weaker but set to recover.

text.p: Zimbabwean shares took a slight knock on Wednesday with losses recorded in a number of blue chips but brokers said this was a temporary hitch and predicted a market recovery on Thursday.
"The market was slightly down on the back of losses in some of the blue chips but generally it's still looking strong and I think it will go up again slightly tomorrow," a broker said.

The 57-counter industrial index shed 2.56 points to close at 10,275.90, largely on the back of a 50 cent loss in blue chip conglomerate Delta which traded in large volumes at 4,450 while retail and hotel giant Meikles eased 15 cents to 2,000, tobacco firm TSL also dropped 15 cents to 775 and National Foods went down 25 cents to 650.

The winners of the day included food and wine producer Cairns and tobacco company BAT, which both added 100 cents to 2,000 and 2,200 respectively while Zimbabwe Newspapers at 3,000 and timber grower and processor Border at 1,000 were 50 cents firmer.

Other gains were in pharmaceutical firm Caps which put on 30 cents to 450, clothing retailer Truworths which went up 25 cents to 1,125 and wood and glass manufacturers PGI and tea and coffee grower EHPL, which both traded 20 cents up. Multi-industrial group TA put on 15 cents to 200.

Minings were more active than of late with nickel producer Bindura up five cents at 850 while coal miners Wankie added 50 to 500 and gold giant Ashanti surged 1,000 cents to 10,000. The seven-counter mining index put on 23.17 points to 1,059.27. -- Stella Mapenzauswa, Harare Newsroom: +263-4 72 52 28/9
